context:
Goal: understand what you built and how well built it is, judged by how it acts for you.
Problem (goal): no view shows you what you see, which parts make it happen, and how healthy each is; only you can say whether that view is worth one audit session.
Based on (measured): claude-settings holds 99 hook files, 110 check scripts, 11 skills and 211 decision records (count 11:37 CST).
Based on (measured): the page copy in git fell about 11 h behind the live page and nothing told you (read 11:30 CST).
Departs from: main docs/map/ (a map written for sessions) — adds one page for you: what you see, what makes it happen, how healthy, measured.
Meanwhile: the retrospective waits for the sync audit and changes nothing.

options.gain: You see each part's health and where it is unmeasured.
options.how: A read-only audit drafts rows; you judge them; a lane builds a tab on this page.
options.label: Build the page (Recommended)
Skip
options.lose: Decay stays hidden until it hurts.

reply: You answered in chat at 11:39 CST (relayed by the retrospective session): "yes i think build it -- let me know if that should be part of the standing artifact or no". It becomes a tab on this page (G14), ruling R34: a read-only audit drafts the rows now, you judge them, a lane builds the tab later. Home: step owner-health-tab.
short: Build a health view of what you built?
title: Should one page show what you see, what makes it happen, and how healthy each part is?
why: No view shows you what you built and how well built it is.
